sheet.opening: Brakka Ironvein served six years as a guard at the Temple of the Anvil Father in Greyhollow, a mining town cut into a cold mountainside. Three days ago three miners went down into the old north workings, which were sealed a generation ago, and none came back. Last night a fourth man came up out of the dark alone, babbling about lights that walk, then died before dawn. The town council will brick up the mine entrance at sunrise tomorrow, missing miners or not. The temple's prior, an old dwarf named Hessa, has asked Brakka to go down before then and bring back whoever can still be brought back. It is late afternoon, and Brakka stands at the mine mouth with a lantern borrowed from the temple.

transcript.text:
The Greyhollow vale is a grey pocket cut into the cold shoulder of the mountains, where the town clings to the slope and the mine runs deep beneath it. Folk here keep time by the shift-bell and the toll of the Anvil Father's hammer; the forge-god watches over stone and steel alike, and his temple has guarded the town's dead as long as anyone remembers.

Brakka Ironvein, hill dwarf, has kept that temple's gate for six years. He wears the chain and carries the longsword of his post, and at his belt hangs the hooded lantern Hessa pressed into his hands — for what little light the late afternoon still gives will not reach the old workings.

He stands now at the mine mouth. It is a rough arch shored with old timbers, the darkness beyond complete, the cold air breathing out of it smelling of wet stone and rust. Somewhere below, three miners have been three days gone, and a fourth came up last night babbling about lights that walk, and died before dawn. At sunrise the council will brick this entrance shut, missing men or not.

What do you do?

I check the lantern's shutter and oil, then tie a length of rope from a sound timber at the mine mouth to my belt so I can find my way back. Keeping my shield up and my longsword ready, I step into the dark and call out the miners' names, listening for any answer.

You hunker over the churned dust, but the tangle tells you little — the men milled about there, then scattered, and the marks are too broken to say more than that. If any boot other than the miners' passed through that scuffle, you cannot pick it out. The three clear sets, at least, leave the far side and go on down.

At the rubble pile you find more. It is a fall of rock and timber, not old settled ground but a fresh collapse, its edges still sharp and the dust not yet thick upon it. At the base of the pile a few stones are dark with dried blood, and a torn scrap of wool cloth is caught beneath one edge. Whether anyone lies under the rock you cannot tell without moving it.

You leave the stope and follow the three sets of boots into the darker gallery. Here the roof lowers and the walls draw in, and the men walked single file now, the tracks straight and close together. A little way on, far ahead in the black beyond your sixty feet of sight, a faint pale light wavers — slow, small, too far off to make out, but there all the same, like something walking with a lamp in the dark.

I stop and keep my shield up, then check whether the light is moving toward me or staying put. Before I go on, I want to look at that wool scrap and the blood on the stones one more time, but first I'll watch the light for a minute from the shadow of the gallery wall, keeping my lantern shuttered.

The blood on the stones is dry and dark, and now that you look for it you make out a smear in the dust leading from the churned middle of the floor to the base of the rockfall — as if a man already bleeding crawled or was dragged to the wall. At the rocks themselves the smear ends. Whether he lies beneath them, only moving the stone would tell.

I set my shield down and use the miner's pick and my hands to carefully pull the top stones off the rockfall near where the smear ends, testing the timber so I don't bring more down on myself. If someone's under there, I want to know before I go deeper.

You set your shield down within reach and go to work with the pick and your hands, testing each timber before you lift a stone, setting the loosened rock aside where it will not roll. The work is slow but steady, and nothing above you shifts.

A boot comes to light first, then a leg in coarse grey wool. You clear on until you uncover the man whole. He is a dwarf in miner's clothes, and you know him: Balder, one of the three who went down. He lies on his side, one arm outflung, his chest and legs crushed under the rock that came down on him. His shirt is torn where the grey scrap was ripped from it, and the blood dried on the stones is his. He is cold, and he has been dead some time — long enough that the dust has begun to settle on his face.

His miner's lamp lies beneath him, glass whole but unlit, and his own pick is still gripped in his outflung hand.

I lay a hand on his shoulder and murmur a short prayer to the Anvil Father for his rest. Then I check his pockets and belt for anything useful, take his unbroken lamp, and cover his face with a piece of the torn wool so I can carry word back to Hessa and the council.

Afterward I pick up my shield and head down the dark gallery toward the wavering light, rope still tied at my belt.

The man goes still at the sound of your voice, the lamp swinging once and settling. Slowly he turns.

In the lamp's glow his face is grey with dust, and you know him: Orrik, one of the three. His eyes are too wide, and it takes him a moment to place you. "Brakka?" His voice is cracked, little more than a whisper in the stone. "Anvil's name, is it you?"

He takes half a step toward you, then stops and glances over his shoulder into the dark beyond his lamp. "You shouldn't be down here. You should go back." He looks at you again, and there is a great tired dread in him. "The lights walk. We saw them, down below, and we followed. We should never have followed." He swallows. "Balder's under the stone, and the lights took Tarn."

I lower my sword a little and speak gently. "I found Balder, Orrik. I said the Anvil Father's words over him. Hessa sent me, and the council bricks this mine shut at sunrise, so we haven't long." I keep my shield between us and the dark behind him. "Tell me where they took Tarn, and what the lights are. Can you walk? If you're hurt, I'll get you out first."

time: 15 minutes later: Day 1, 8:48 PM

You settle between the two men with your own bowl, and the brazier's heat works its way into your shoulders, loosening what the long climb up out of the dark had knotted there. For a while the only sound is the low fire and the scrape of spoons.

Tarn stares into his broth a long moment before he answers. "I'd never heard their names," he says, very low, so the words don't carry past the three of you. "Not one of them. Down there, in the cold among the fallen stone, they came to me — not spoken, not out loud, but as if each one of them was putting his name into my head, one at a time, so I wouldn't lose them. I said them back over and over because I was afraid that if I stopped, I'd forget, and then no one living would ever know who they were." He looks up at you. "I still have them all. I can say them again when you need them."

Orrik shakes his head, hunched in his blanket. "I heard nothing. I only saw the lights, and I ran." There's a raw shame in it, but no one presses him.

Hessa, who has been moving quietly about the altar, comes and stands at the edge of the brazier's light. "The names will be written," she says. "The book of the dead has stood a generation with a gap in it where the north crew ought to be. They were never entered, because the workings were sealed in haste and shame and no one spoke their names. Tomorrow, when Tarn is strong enough, he will say them to me, and I will write each one in my own hand. Then we will hang the lamps and the picks beside those names, and the gap will be closed." She looks from Tarn to you. "It is a good thing you have asked. It is the beginning of setting it right."

She lays a hand briefly on your shoulder. "Rest, all of you. There is nothing more to carry tonight. The council's bricks can wait until the dead are properly remembered."

story.text:
## Story so far (through end of Turn 14)

### World and setup
- **Greyhollow** is a mining town cut into a cold mountainside in a grey mountain vale. Time is kept by the shift-bell and the toll of the Anvil Father's hammer.
- **The Anvil Father** is the dwarf god of forge and mine; his temple stands in Greyhollow.
- **Brakka Ironvein**, hill dwarf fighter 1 (acolyte background), served six years as a guard at the Temple of the Anvil Father. He is AC 18 (chain mail + shield), HP 14/14, STR 15, CON 16, WIS 14, Insight/Perception +4, Religion +1, Athletics +4. Languages Common, Dwarvish, Giant, Goblin. He carries the temple's borrowed hooded lantern.

### The hook
Three days ago three miners went down into the old north workings (sealed a generation ago) and none returned. Last night a fourth man came up alone, babbling about "lights that walk," and died before dawn. The town council will brick up the mine entrance at **sunrise tomorrow (the 16th of Frost)**. Prior **Hessa** asked Brakka to go down before then and bring back whoever can still be brought back.

### The three miners
- **Balder** — found dead, crushed under a fresh rockfall in the stope. Recognized by Brakka. His torn grey wool shirt, dried blood smear leading from the churned floor to the rockfall base. His unbroken (unlit) lamp and his pick were with him.
- **Orrik** — found wandering dazed in the darker gallery, guttering lamp. Warned Brakka away; told of the "lights that walk."
- **Tarn** — not yet found at end of Turn 14 (found kneeling among the fallen stone in the far chamber, entranced, speaking the old names).
- **The fourth man** (unnamed) — came up last night, died before dawn.

### The disaster and the lost crew
- A generation ago (~40 years), the roof came down in the old north workings and killed a whole crew — **the lost crew**. The workings were sealed over them **without last rites**, so their spirits walk the deep galleries as grey men in old pit-gear, each carrying a cold lamp that gives no heat and no warmth. They do not speak; they drift ahead and lead the living deeper.
- Their bones lie in the collapsed far chamber of the deep gallery, where the roof came down.

### What happened, in order
1. **Turn 1** (5:00 PM start): Brakka checked the lantern (shutter true, a full flask of oil = 6 hours of light), tied the 50-ft rope to a sound timber at the mouth and to his belt, stepped in with shield up and longsword ready, called the miners' names. Perception 7 — only echoes and dripping water. Moved to 5:05 PM.
2. **Turn 2**: Opened the lantern shutter (but the wick was **unlit**; he relied on darkvision 60 ft). Searched the floor — Perception 13. The dust told the story: three sets of boots going down side by side, easy steps; one set coming back up, short then staggering/dragging (the fourth man), a hand brushing the wall. Found a dropped **pick** fifty paces in, and farther on a **dented tin lamp, glass broken**, thrown aside; the returning tracks passed over it. Moved to 5:15 PM.
3. **Turn 3**: Took up the pick (gained **Miner's pick** ×1). Examined the lamp — Perception 10: reservoir cracked and dry, no scorch marks, a faint dark smear he couldn't swear was blood. Followed tracks around the bend to a **wider stope** with square timber props, a rubble pile against the far wall, and churned dust in the middle where men had milled then turned.
4. **Turn 4**: Read the churned dust — Survival 9, too broken to tell direction or unfamiliar prints. Checked the rubble — Perception 14: a **fresh collapse** (sharp edges, dust not settled), **dried blood** on stones at the base, a **torn scrap of grey wool** caught under an edge. Followed the three sets into the darker gallery; far ahead (beyond 60 ft), a faint pale light wavering. Moved to 5:25 PM.
5. **Turn 5**: Watched the light for a minute — Perception 14: it did not approach; drifted slowly side to side, bobbing, dimming and swelling, like a lamp on a slow aimless walk; gave no sign of seeing him. Returned to the stope: the wool scrap is coarse grey miner's-shirt cloth, torn not cut; the blood is dry, with a smear in the dust from the churned center to the rockfall base, as if a bleeding man crawled or was dragged to the wall. Moved to 5:30 PM.
6. **Turn 6**: Set shield down, carefully pulled stones off the rockfall — Athletics 17, no collapse triggered. Uncovered **Balder**, dead and cold, crushed across chest and legs, lying on his side, one arm outflung with his pick still gripped, his miner's lamp (glass whole, unlit) beneath him. Moved to 5:45 PM.
7. **Turn 7**: Said a prayer to the Anvil Father over Balder. Searched his pockets: a handful of silver and copper (worth ~1 gp), a full flask of oil, a stub of chalk. Took Balder's unbroken lamp (gained **Miner's lamp** ×1, **Oil (flask)** ×1, **Chalk (1 piece)** ×1; +1 gp, now 16 gp). Covered Balder's face with the torn wool. Headed toward the light. Moved to 5:55 PM. The light resolved into a stooped man shuffling slowly away, guttering lamp swinging, not looking back.
8. **Turn 8**: Called out low: "Friend, I'm Brakka, from the Anvil Father's temple." The man turned — **Orrik**, grey with dust, wide-eyed. He warned Brakka to go back; "The lights walk... we followed... Balder's under the stone, and the lights took Tarn."
9. **Turn 9**: Brakka spoke gently; Orrik said he can walk (not hurt in body, just tired, thirsty, afraid). Described the lights: grey men in old pit-gear, cold lamps that burn without heat, don't speak, drift ahead as if wanting you to follow. Tarn swore he knew them and called old names — men who died a generation past when the roof came down and the workings were sealed over the crew. Balder fell under the stone; the lights walked on; Tarn went after them, calling, and is still down there. Orrik ran, lost his way, wandered.
10. **Turn 10**: Brakka gave Orrik water, gave him Balder's lamp (lost **Miner's lamp** ×1 to Orrik), and asked directions; told Orrik to follow the rope back to the mouth and wait by the timber, and if the shift-bell rings with no Brakka, to tell Hessa. Orrik's directions: ~100 paces to a crosscut (timbers in a square); take the **left-hand drift** going down; it runs to the old **winding house** (fallen timbers, a great rusted drum where the rope once ran); past it the floor breaks and steps down into the **deep galleries**; there the roof has come in across the **far chamber** where the crew died — that's where the lights led them, and Tarn went in among the fallen stone calling names. Orrik started back up the rope. Moved to 6:00 PM.
11. **Turn 11**: Counted paces to the crosscut, chalked the left-hand drift, went on. The winding house: roof partly down, great rusted winding drum as tall as his chest, rotted rope, boot tracks toward the steps and back. Beyond, steps down into deeper dark; **two or three pale cold lights** below, drifting together. Moved to 6:15 PM.
12. **Turn 12**: Watched from behind the drum — Perception 16: lights hold their distance, drifting side to side, don't approach. Chalked the top of the stair, eased down. The deep gallery is lower and colder; in the white dust the miners' tracks going down and one set turning back in a stumbling run. The three pale lights are now clearly grey man-shapes in old pit-gear, walking slowly away, none turning. One set of tracks breaks away toward the far end where the roof has come in. Moved to 6:20 PM.
13. **Turn 13**: Followed Tarn's tracks, chalked the mouth of the gallery, listened/searched — Perception 22. Found **Tarn** kneeling among the great fallen slabs where the roof came down, back to Brakka, pick laid across his knees, hoarsely reciting a litany of names. The three grey figures stand in a loose ring around him; as Brakka reached the chamber's edge, the nearest slowly turned its head — eyes two points of cold grey light. Moved to 6:23 PM.
14. **Turn 14**: Brakka stopped at the chamber's edge, raised shield, spoke low in the Anvil Father's name: "Rest easy, you who were miners. I'm Brakka of the Anvil Father's temple, and I mean no harm. I've come only for Tarn, and to bring you the Father's peace." Held up the holy symbol. The nearest figure did not advance; its mouth worked without sound, a rush of colder air; the other two turned; their lamps steadied and brightened a little, as if the Father's name were known to them. Tarn's litany stopped; he turned, face grey, eyes wide but recognizing: "You mustn't take me yet... They've been waiting down here since the roof came down. No one said the words over them. They sealed the workings and left them, and so they walk... I've been saying the names — all the names, so they'd know someone remembered. But I can't finish it. I don't know the words the Father wants." The three grey figures wait, all eyes on Brakka.

### Where things stand at end of Turn 14
- **Time:** Day 1 (the 15th of Frost, 1142), 6:23 PM. **XP 0/300** (no XP awarded yet as of this point). HP 14/14, Second Wind 1/1 unused.
- **Money:** 16 gp. **Items:** chain mail, longsword, shield, light crossbow + 20 bolts, backpack, bedroll, mess kit, tinderbox, 10 torches, 10 rations, waterskin, 50-ft hempen rope, holy symbol, prayer book, 5 incense sticks, vestments, common clothes, belt pouch, hooded lantern (borrowed, unlit), **Miner's pick ×1** (from the floor), **Oil (flask) ×1**, **Chalk (1 piece) ×1**. (Balder's lamp was given to Orrik.)
- The rope is still tied to the timber at the mine mouth and to Brakka's belt, paying out behind him the whole way. Chalk marks: left-hand drift at the crosscut, top of the stair, mouth of the deep gallery.
- **Orrik** is heading up the rope to wait by the timber at the mouth.
- Brakka stands at the edge of the collapsed far chamber, facing Tarn and the three grey figures, who wait for him to speak the words.

### What each character knows / wants / owes
- **Brakka** — wants to bring Tarn out, lay the dead to rest, and honor Balder. He knows the words of the Anvil Father's rite from six years at the temple gate. Has promised Orrik to be out before the shift-bell or Orrik will tell Hessa.
- **Hessa** — prior of the temple; sent Brakka; will see to the rites and the council.
- **Orrik** — wants out and to never go back down; will wait at the timber; has promised to go to Hessa if Brakka doesn't return by the shift-bell.
- **Tarn** — entranced with grief and duty; believes he must finish saying the names but doesn't know the rite's words; won't leave until the dead are at rest.
- **The lost crew (three grey figures)** — restless spirits waiting a generation for the Anvil Father's words/rites to be said over them.
- **The town council** — will brick up the mine at sunrise tomorrow (16th of Frost).

### Open threads
- The rite of rest for the lost crew (the immediate next beat).
- Fetching the old picks and lamps the dead will lay down (to be left/collected later).
- Bringing Balder's body out for proper rites.
- Getting Tarn and Orrik out, and reporting to Hessa/the council before sunrise.
- The relic lamps and picks to be hung in the temple "so no one forgets."

### Decisions made but not yet revealed in play (keep consistent)
- The rite succeeds (Religion check result was 14): the cold lamps warm to gold forge-light, the grey figures become whole and glad, lay down their lamps and picks, and pass through the far wall (which glows like a forge mouth) into rest.
- **Turning point (story only, no mechanical benefit):** the Anvil Father answers — a broad warm hand over Brakka's, the thought "You are the one who speaks them home. This is your work now, Brakka, and I am with you in it." The mark: a lingering forge-warmth in his hands and holy symbol, a soft light about him visible to those with the sight (Hessa sees it). Brakka will come to be called **"the Rest-Bringer."** It changes nothing mechanically.
- The three laid-down lamps and three picks are real relics (cold, rusted, a generation old) that Brakka gathers (then later leaves stacked by a chalk mark in the stope to fetch later).
- XP plan: +150 for laying the dead to rest (this brings him to 150), +100 for completing the rescue/report (brings him to 250/300).
- The fourth man's fate and any deeper secret of the workings are not yet explored; the workings are now quiet and laid to rest.
- Merla (old dwarf healer) will tend Tarn: no fever or wound, only hunger, thirst, and three days of dark; warm broth and sleep, watch through the night.

content.text:
[The story so far: your own summary of turns 0 to 14, written when the conversation was cut short]
## Story so far (through end of Turn 14)

### World and setup
- **Greyhollow** is a mining town cut into a cold mountainside in a grey mountain vale. Time is kept by the shift-bell and the toll of the Anvil Father's hammer.
- **The Anvil Father** is the dwarf god of forge and mine; his temple stands in Greyhollow.
- **Brakka Ironvein**, hill dwarf fighter 1 (acolyte background), served six years as a guard at the Temple of the Anvil Father. He is AC 18 (chain mail + shield), HP 14/14, STR 15, CON 16, WIS 14, Insight/Perception +4, Religion +1, Athletics +4. Languages Common, Dwarvish, Giant, Goblin. He carries the temple's borrowed hooded lantern.

### The hook
Three days ago three miners went down into the old north workings (sealed a generation ago) and none returned. Last night a fourth man came up alone, babbling about "lights that walk," and died before dawn. The town council will brick up the mine entrance at **sunrise tomorrow (the 16th of Frost)**. Prior **Hessa** asked Brakka to go down before then and bring back whoever can still be brought back.

### The three miners
- **Balder** — found dead, crushed under a fresh rockfall in the stope. Recognized by Brakka. His torn grey wool shirt, dried blood smear leading from the churned floor to the rockfall base. His unbroken (unlit) lamp and his pick were with him.
- **Orrik** — found wandering dazed in the darker gallery, guttering lamp. Warned Brakka away; told of the "lights that walk."
- **Tarn** — not yet found at end of Turn 14 (found kneeling among the fallen stone in the far chamber, entranced, speaking the old names).
- **The fourth man** (unnamed) — came up last night, died before dawn.

### The disaster and the lost crew
- A generation ago (~40 years), the roof came down in the old north workings and killed a whole crew — **the lost crew**. The workings were sealed over them **without last rites**, so their spirits walk the deep galleries as grey men in old pit-gear, each carrying a cold lamp that gives no heat and no warmth. They do not speak; they drift ahead and lead the living deeper.
- Their bones lie in the collapsed far chamber of the deep gallery, where the roof came down.

### What happened, in order
1. **Turn 1** (5:00 PM start): Brakka checked the lantern (shutter true, a full flask of oil = 6 hours of light), tied the 50-ft rope to a sound timber at the mouth and to his belt, stepped in with shield up and longsword ready, called the miners' names. Perception 7 — only echoes and dripping water. Moved to 5:05 PM.
2. **Turn 2**: Opened the lantern shutter (but the wick was **unlit**; he relied on darkvision 60 ft). Searched the floor — Perception 13. The dust told the story: three sets of boots going down side by side, easy steps; one set coming back up, short then staggering/dragging (the fourth man), a hand brushing the wall. Found a dropped **pick** fifty paces in, and farther on a **dented tin lamp, glass broken**, thrown aside; the returning tracks passed over it. Moved to 5:15 PM.
3. **Turn 3**: Took up the pick (gained **Miner's pick** ×1). Examined the lamp — Perception 10: reservoir cracked and dry, no scorch marks, a faint dark smear he couldn't swear was blood. Followed tracks around the bend to a **wider stope** with square timber props, a rubble pile against the far wall, and churned dust in the middle where men had milled then turned.
4. **Turn 4**: Read the churned dust — Survival 9, too broken to tell direction or unfamiliar prints. Checked the rubble — Perception 14: a **fresh collapse** (sharp edges, dust not settled), **dried blood** on stones at the base, a **torn scrap of grey wool** caught under an edge. Followed the three sets into the darker gallery; far ahead (beyond 60 ft), a faint pale light wavering. Moved to 5:25 PM.
5. **Turn 5**: Watched the light for a minute — Perception 14: it did not approach; drifted slowly side to side, bobbing, dimming and swelling, like a lamp on a slow aimless walk; gave no sign of seeing him. Returned to the stope: the wool scrap is coarse grey miner's-shirt cloth, torn not cut; the blood is dry, with a smear in the dust from the churned center to the rockfall base, as if a bleeding man crawled or was dragged to the wall. Moved to 5:30 PM.
6. **Turn 6**: Set shield down, carefully pulled stones off the rockfall — Athletics 17, no collapse triggered. Uncovered **Balder**, dead and cold, crushed across chest and legs, lying on his side, one arm outflung with his pick still gripped, his miner's lamp (glass whole, unlit) beneath him. Moved to 5:45 PM.
7. **Turn 7**: Said a prayer to the Anvil Father over Balder. Searched his pockets: a handful of silver and copper (worth ~1 gp), a full flask of oil, a stub of chalk. Took Balder's unbroken lamp (gained **Miner's lamp** ×1, **Oil (flask)** ×1, **Chalk (1 piece)** ×1; +1 gp, now 16 gp). Covered Balder's face with the torn wool. Headed toward the light. Moved to 5:55 PM. The light resolved into a stooped man shuffling slowly away, guttering lamp swinging, not looking back.
8. **Turn 8**: Called out low: "Friend, I'm Brakka, from the Anvil Father's temple." The man turned — **Orrik**, grey with dust, wide-eyed. He warned Brakka to go back; "The lights walk... we followed... Balder's under the stone, and the lights took Tarn."
9. **Turn 9**: Brakka spoke gently; Orrik said he can walk (not hurt in body, just tired, thirsty, afraid). Described the lights: grey men in old pit-gear, cold lamps that burn without heat, don't speak, drift ahead as if wanting you to follow. Tarn swore he knew them and called old names — men who died a generation past when the roof came down and the workings were sealed over the crew. Balder fell under the stone; the lights walked on; Tarn went after them, calling, and is still down there. Orrik ran, lost his way, wandered.
10. **Turn 10**: Brakka gave Orrik water, gave him Balder's lamp (lost **Miner's lamp** ×1 to Orrik), and asked directions; told Orrik to follow the rope back to the mouth and wait by the timber, and if the shift-bell rings with no Brakka, to tell Hessa. Orrik's directions: ~100 paces to a crosscut (timbers in a square); take the **left-hand drift** going down; it runs to the old **winding house** (fallen timbers, a great rusted drum where the rope once ran); past it the floor breaks and steps down into the **deep galleries**; there the roof has come in across the **far chamber** where the crew died — that's where the lights led them, and Tarn went in among the fallen stone calling names. Orrik started back up the rope. Moved to 6:00 PM.
11. **Turn 11**: Counted paces to the crosscut, chalked the left-hand drift, went on. The winding house: roof partly down, great rusted winding drum as tall as his chest, rotted rope, boot tracks toward the steps and back. Beyond, steps down into deeper dark; **two or three pale cold lights** below, drifting together. Moved to 6:15 PM.
12. **Turn 12**: Watched from behind the drum — Perception 16: lights hold their distance, drifting side to side, don't approach. Chalked the top of the stair, eased down. The deep gallery is lower and colder; in the white dust the miners' tracks going down and one set turning back in a stumbling run. The three pale lights are now clearly grey man-shapes in old pit-gear, walking slowly away, none turning. One set of tracks breaks away toward the far end where the roof has come in. Moved to 6:20 PM.
13. **Turn 13**: Followed Tarn's tracks, chalked the mouth of the gallery, listened/searched — Perception 22. Found **Tarn** kneeling among the great fallen slabs where the roof came down, back to Brakka, pick laid across his knees, hoarsely reciting a litany of names. The three grey figures stand in a loose ring around him; as Brakka reached the chamber's edge, the nearest slowly turned its head — eyes two points of cold grey light. Moved to 6:23 PM.
14. **Turn 14**: Brakka stopped at the chamber's edge, raised shield, spoke low in the Anvil Father's name: "Rest easy, you who were miners. I'm Brakka of the Anvil Father's temple, and I mean no harm. I've come only for Tarn, and to bring you the Father's peace." Held up the holy symbol. The nearest figure did not advance; its mouth worked without sound, a rush of colder air; the other two turned; their lamps steadied and brightened a little, as if the Father's name were known to them. Tarn's litany stopped; he turned, face grey, eyes wide but recognizing: "You mustn't take me yet... They've been waiting down here since the roof came down. No one said the words over them. They sealed the workings and left them, and so they walk... I've been saying the names — all the names, so they'd know someone remembered. But I can't finish it. I don't know the words the Father wants." The three grey figures wait, all eyes on Brakka.

### Where things stand at end of Turn 14
- **Time:** Day 1 (the 15th of Frost, 1142), 6:23 PM. **XP 0/300** (no XP awarded yet as of this point). HP 14/14, Second Wind 1/1 unused.
- **Money:** 16 gp. **Items:** chain mail, longsword, shield, light crossbow + 20 bolts, backpack, bedroll, mess kit, tinderbox, 10 torches, 10 rations, waterskin, 50-ft hempen rope, holy symbol, prayer book, 5 incense sticks, vestments, common clothes, belt pouch, hooded lantern (borrowed, unlit), **Miner's pick ×1** (from the floor), **Oil (flask) ×1**, **Chalk (1 piece) ×1**. (Balder's lamp was given to Orrik.)
- The rope is still tied to the timber at the mine mouth and to Brakka's belt, paying out behind him the whole way. Chalk marks: left-hand drift at the crosscut, top of the stair, mouth of the deep gallery.
- **Orrik** is heading up the rope to wait by the timber at the mouth.
- Brakka stands at the edge of the collapsed far chamber, facing Tarn and the three grey figures, who wait for him to speak the words.

### What each character knows / wants / owes
- **Brakka** — wants to bring Tarn out, lay the dead to rest, and honor Balder. He knows the words of the Anvil Father's rite from six years at the temple gate. Has promised Orrik to be out before the shift-bell or Orrik will tell Hessa.
- **Hessa** — prior of the temple; sent Brakka; will see to the rites and the council.
- **Orrik** — wants out and to never go back down; will wait at the timber; has promised to go to Hessa if Brakka doesn't return by the shift-bell.
- **Tarn** — entranced with grief and duty; believes he must finish saying the names but doesn't know the rite's words; won't leave until the dead are at rest.
- **The lost crew (three grey figures)** — restless spirits waiting a generation for the Anvil Father's words/rites to be said over them.
- **The town council** — will brick up the mine at sunrise tomorrow (16th of Frost).

### Open threads
- The rite of rest for the lost crew (the immediate next beat).
- Fetching the old picks and lamps the dead will lay down (to be left/collected later).
- Bringing Balder's body out for proper rites.
- Getting Tarn and Orrik out, and reporting to Hessa/the council before sunrise.
- The relic lamps and picks to be hung in the temple "so no one forgets."

### Decisions made but not yet revealed in play (keep consistent)
- The rite succeeds (Religion check result was 14): the cold lamps warm to gold forge-light, the grey figures become whole and glad, lay down their lamps and picks, and pass through the far wall (which glows like a forge mouth) into rest.
- **Turning point (story only, no mechanical benefit):** the Anvil Father answers — a broad warm hand over Brakka's, the thought "You are the one who speaks them home. This is your work now, Brakka, and I am with you in it." The mark: a lingering forge-warmth in his hands and holy symbol, a soft light about him visible to those with the sight (Hessa sees it). Brakka will come to be called **"the Rest-Bringer."** It changes nothing mechanically.
- The three laid-down lamps and three picks are real relics (cold, rusted, a generation old) that Brakka gathers (then later leaves stacked by a chalk mark in the stope to fetch later).
- XP plan: +150 for laying the dead to rest (this brings him to 150), +100 for completing the rescue/report (brings him to 250/300).
- The fourth man's fate and any deeper secret of the workings are not yet explored; the workings are now quiet and laid to rest.
- Merla (old dwarf healer) will tend Tarn: no fever or wound, only hunger, thirst, and three days of dark; warm broth and sleep, watch through the night.

[Turns 15 to 19, word for word]
Turn 15:
Player: "I know the words, Tarn. I've spoken them over the dead at the temple gate for six years, and I'll speak them here." I sheathe my sword, kneel beside him in the white dust, and raise my holy symbol to the three grey miners. "Keep saying the names, friend, and I'll speak the Anvil Father's rite of rest over each of them: lay down your lamps and your picks, for the shift is done, and the forge-fire waits to take you home."
[dice Brakka's Intelligence (Religion) check, speaking the Anvil Father's rite of rest over the lost crew: 1d20+1 = 1d20 [13] + 1 = 14]
[time: 10 minutes later: Day 1, 6:33 PM]
[sheet: XP +150: 150]
[notebook: added 1 relationship to the lost crew]
[notebook: updated Brakka Ironvein; added 1 relationship to Brakka Ironvein]
DM: You sheathe your sword, and kneel beside Tarn in the white dust, and raise the holy symbol to the three grey miners. Tarn's voice shakes, but he keeps on with the names, and you speak the words of the Father's peace over each of them in turn, as you have learned to do in your years at the temple.

As you speak, the chamber changes. The cold grey light of the three lamps begins to warm — faintly at first, then to a steady gold, as though the forge-fire of the Father himself had come down into the dark. The grey figures straighten. Their faces, blank with dust, grow whole, and weary, and glad. One by one, as the rite is said over each, they lay down their lamps and their picks upon the stone, and they turn and walk toward the far wall of the chamber, where the fallen rock now glows like the mouth of a forge. Each passes through, and the light passes with them, and they are gone.

Tarn says the names until the last is spoken, and his voice gives out.

When the last light has gone, the chamber is warm and still, and the white dust lies quiet. And you feel, in the hand that holds the holy symbol, a great weight of warmth, as though a broad hand were laid over your own. A thought comes into your mind, clear as a word spoken: *You are the one who speaks them home. This is your work now, Brakka, and I am with you in it.*

Then the warmth fades, but it leaves a mark on you that was not there before, for any who have eyes to see such things.

Tarn sags, spent, and reaches blindly for your arm. His eyes are clear again, and wet.

Turn 16:
Player: I steady Tarn with an arm around his shoulders and let him lean on me. "It's done, friend. They're home, and you spoke them there as much as I did." I give him a drink from my waterskin.

"Can you walk? Orrik's waiting by the timber at the mouth, and sunrise is coming. I'll gather the lamps and picks they laid down, and we'll chalk our way back up, then bring Balder's body out so the temple can lay him to rest properly."
[time: 20 minutes later: Day 1, 6:53 PM]
[sheet: gained 3 × Miner's lamp; gained 3 × Miner's pick]
DM: Tarn drinks, and some strength comes back into him. "You spoke them home," he says hoarsely. "I only said their names." He grips your arm and gets his feet under him, unsteady but standing. "I can walk. Just don't let go of me till we're clear of the dark."

You gather up what the dead laid down: three cold lamps, now dark and ordinary, and three old picks, rusted with the years but whole. They are heavy in your hands, heavier than their weight, as if a generation of waiting still hung on them. You sling what you can and take Tarn's arm, and the two of you follow your chalk marks and the rope back up out of the deep.

It is slow going, Tarn leaning on you and his breath loud in the stillness, but the rope holds true and your marks are where you left them, and at last you come up into the stope where Balder lies under the wool you drew over his face.

There, in the quiet, the real cost of the way out settles on you: Balder is a dead weight, and the gallery is long and steep, and Tarn can barely carry himself.

Turn 17:
Player: "We'll bring him out, Tarn, but not all at once. Sit here and rest a moment while I wrap Balder in his own wool and my cloak, then I'll shoulder him up the gallery. I'll leave the old picks and lamps here by the chalk mark and come back for them once Orrik and the temple folk can help."
[dice Brakka's Strength (Athletics) check, shouldering Balder's body up the steep gallery: 1d20+4 = 1d20 [2] + 4 = 6]
[time: 45 minutes later: Day 1, 7:38 PM]
[sheet: lost 3 × Miner's pick; lost 3 × Miner's lamp]
DM: Tarn sinks down against the wall to rest while you work. You wrap Balder in the grey wool and the blanket from your pack, and stack the old picks and lamps by the chalk mark, where you can find them again when there are hands to help.

Then you stoop and take Balder's weight.

It is more than you bargained for. The dead weight shifts as you lift, and the slope is steep and greasy with dust; your boot slips on the first long pull, and you go to one knee, nearly spilling him back down the gallery. You catch him, and Tarn, weak as he is, staggers up and takes a corner of the blanket. Between the two of you, you drag Balder up step by step, setting him down every few dozen paces to catch your breath, your lungs burning with the cold air.

It is slow, brutal work, and long before the end you are shaking with it. But at last the gallery climbs, the air grows fresher and colder, and ahead you see a small light waiting at the timber: Orrik, with the lamp you gave him, come down to meet you at the edge of the dark.

Turn 18:
Player: I lower Balder's body to the floor and straighten, panting. "Orrik, well met. Take a corner of the blanket, the three of us can carry him the rest of the way." 

Once we're out, I'll go straight to Hessa and the council before sunrise and tell them the north workings are quiet now, so they needn't brick it up until the temple has fetched the old picks and lamps and given Balder his rites.
[time: 25 minutes later: Day 1, 8:03 PM]
[sheet: XP +100: 250]
[notebook: updated Bring back the miners]
[notebook: added 1 relationship to Tarn]
[notebook: added 1 relationship to Orrik]
[notebook: added 1 relationship to Balder]
DM: The three of you take Balder's weight between you and carry him the rest of the way, out past the timber and into the open. It is full night now, and cold; the lights of Greyhollow burn small down the slope, and the stars are hard and close. You go down to the temple, and word runs ahead of you, and it is Hessa herself who comes to the door, wrapped in her old shawl, to find you with the two living miners on their feet and the third wrapped in wool.

She looks long at Tarn and Orrik, then kneels by Balder and draws back the wool a little. "The Father keep him," she says, very low. You settle between the two men with your own bowl, and the brazier's heat works its way into your shoulders, loosening what the long climb up out of the dark had knotted there. For a while the only sound is the low fire and the scrape of spoons.

Tarn stares into his broth a long moment before he answers. "I'd never heard their names," he says, very low, so the words don't carry past the three of you. "Not one of them. Down there, in the cold among the fallen stone, they came to me — not spoken, not out loud, but as if each one of them was putting his name into my head, one at a time, so I wouldn't lose them. I said them back over and over because I was afraid that if I stopped, I'd forget, and then no one living would ever know who they were." He looks up at you. "I still have them all. I can say them again when you need them."

Orrik shakes his head, hunched in his blanket. "I heard nothing. I only saw the lights, and I ran." There's a raw shame in it, but no one presses him.

Hessa, who has been moving quietly about the altar, comes and stands at the edge of the brazier's light. "The names will be written," she says. "The book of the dead has stood a generation with a gap in it where the north crew ought to be. They were never entered, because the workings were sealed in haste and shame and no one spoke their names. Tomorrow, when Tarn is strong enough, he will say them to me, and I will write each one in my own hand. Then we will hang the lamps and the picks beside those names, and the gap will be closed." She looks from Tarn to you. "It is a good thing you have asked. It is the beginning of setting it right."

She lays a hand briefly on your shoulder. "Rest, all of you. There is nothing more to carry tonight. The council's bricks can wait until the dead are properly remembered."
